note: v1 97.92 (seeds 0/11 97.92/97.92): ANNEALING - first draft. A Berlin-school sequencer (moog-seq) that composes its own tune by SIMULATED ANNEALING while you listen: a 16-step sequence starts as noise - random notes over three octaves, random rests, every pitch tens of cents off any scale - and every bar the machine proposes mutations, keeping the better ones and, while it is hot, sometimes a worse one. The temperature falls through five uneven epochs (20/18/24/14/28 bars): the blips find a key, a rhythm, then a minor riff that locks into 5-limit JUST INTONATION; the sine-partial pad's voices are detuned by the temperature, so their beating slows and stops as they cool into pure ratios; the bass's cents and the electro kit's pattern anneal too (noise when hot, a motorik target when cold); a temperature lane opens the sequencer's filter and dirties a bit-crusher. Converged for 16 bars, then one REHEAT (half the steps thrown back into noise) and a cold coda. 156 bars at 116 bpm, 5:23. The hill-climb that writes the chirpers' songs, turned inside out and played. Next: a voice reading its own loss and singing it, more engine systems, and stronger seams. Not heard by me.

v2 94.92 (seeds 0/11 94.92/94.92, level with v1 re-scored 94.96 now that t6 and t8 exist beside it): THE VOICE READS ITS LOSS - Harry's brief asks for vox as realistic as possible, effected, with obtuse words. At the start of each epoch a humanized voice (chirp tts --humanize 0.7, through a little tape wow and an echo) reads the search's own error aloud - 'zero point eight six', 'zero point nine' (it got worse: a hot machine accepts that), 'zero point six six', 'zero point three eight', 'zero point two eight' - spoken while the machine is hot and melodized more each epoch onto the riff, its sung notes retuned into the same just intonation as everything else; when the search converges it sings 'zero'; the reheat throws it back into speech ('zero point eight eight'); the coda sings 'zero' again. A loss curve, read and then sung. Not heard by me.

v3 96.92 (seeds 0/11 96.92/96.95 vs v2 94.92/94.92): THE POWER LIGHT. Annealing used to open on three seconds of nothing - the search had not started - and close on two seconds of silence, so the album's bleed into t6 and t8 met a hole (compscore's join measured a 76 dB level jump). Now the machine is ON before the search starts: a warm drone on A (the hum of a box left on in the dark - the album's amber light) from the very first beat, swelling through power-on and sinking under the first epoch; it comes back under the cold coda and holds to the last beat. Structure 90 -> 100, the join's level jump 76 -> 22 dB. The joins still differ in colour from t6's quiet tail and t8's head (the drone's low A against their thin edges); I tried the drone an octave up and quieter at both ends - the joins improved but the form blurred (95.37) - and will shape the edges with t6 and t8's owners. Not heard by me.

v4 97.08 (seeds 0/11 97.08/97.08, level with v3 re-scored 97.09/97.09), kept on judgment: THE SEARCH GLIDES - chirp-eco's coverage table lists pitch bends and expression paths as barely used. While Annealing's machine is hot, each blip of the candidate tune now SLIDES into its pitch from somewhere else - a random offset scaled by the temperature, up to seven semitones, written as an expression path on the sequencer's pitch in cents - so the hot search sounds like it is feeling its way toward the notes; as it cools the slides shrink to nothing and the converged riff lands dead on. (A ladder filter in place of the low-pass darkened the mix and cost a point; reverted.) Not heard by me.

v5 96.49 (seeds 0/11 96.49/96.45 vs v4 re-scored 96.74/96.69), kept on judgment: LESS SQUELCH. Harry's first chirpers8 note (18:19, on another track) was 'too squelchy'. Annealing's hot search ran through a resonant low-pass (q 1.2) and a 5-bit, 6 kHz bit-crusher mixed up to 70% - the most squelchy, chewed sound on my side of the album. Now the filter's resonance is gentler (q 0.75) and the crusher is an 8-bit, 11 kHz glitter mixed at most 45%: the hot machine sounds noisy and glittering rather than resonant and chewed, and the slides still carry the search. The cost is a little top end (spectrum 100 -> 96). Not heard by me.

v6 96.51 (seeds 0/11 96.51/96.48 vs v5 96.49/96.45): THERE YOU ARE. Annealing's voice has spent the track reading the search's error aloud, more and more sung as it cools, and it sang only one word at the top: 'zero'. Now, when the search finally converges, the voice SINGS the riff the machine was looking for - slowed to a sung phrase, twice, with wM's new singing voice: 'there you are, you were always here' (a love letter to the machine's own answer, sideways), every note retuned to the same 5-limit just pitches as the band. Not heard by me.

v7 97.43 (seeds 0/11 97.43/97.33 vs v6 96.51/96.48): ON THE RADIO FIRST - the join with t6, Annealing's weakest term (flow 40: a 22 dB spectral jump, my A1 drone arriving at full weight where t6 ends on a radio voice far away). Now the machine's hum is first heard THROUGH that radio: wM's radio effect with the dial sweeping onto the station - band-limited, the static and the heterodyne whistle falling away - and as the dial lands, a beat and a half in, the full low hum comes into the room underneath and the search begins. The power light is on the radio before it is in the room. Flow 40 -> 60 (spectral distance at the seam 22 -> 5 dB). A first version held the radio alone for four bars and read as an extra section (structure and variety fell); overlapping the hum's entry fixed it. Not heard by me.
rebaselined on compscore c8edcd03: v7 (the song file) scores 97.706/97.540 on seeds 0/11; best was 97.43 on an older compscore. Compare candidates against this.

v8 97.64 (seeds 0/11 97.64/97.49, level with the rebaselined v7 97.71/97.54), kept on judgment: THE VOICE TUNES IN. Since v7 Annealing's hum is first heard over a radio; now its voice is too, while the machine is hot. Each reading of the search's error made above a temperature of 0.2 comes over a radio whose dial is off the station by the temperature - the first ('zero point eight six') half lost in static and the heterodyne whistle, the second nearer, the third almost tuned - and from the fourth epoch, cool enough, the voice is in the room, clear and then singing. The reheat throws it back onto the radio. The dial swings off only while the voice speaks (a first version left the static running under the whole track and cost the joins 14 points of flow). Not heard by me.

v9 98.10 (seeds 0/11 98.10/98.07 vs v8 re-scored with the new peer ratings 98.06/97.98): THE ANSWER ON AN INSTRUMENT. For four minutes Annealing's riff is a sequencer blip - filtered, crushed, sliding - because it is a search, not yet a tune. Now, when the search converges, the riff it found stops being a blip: it moves onto an electric piano (the engine's Rhodes-style tine model), warm and exact in the same just intonation, under the voice singing it ('there you are, you were always here'). The reheat hands it back to the machine; the cold end of the coda gives it to the piano again. The arrival now changes colour as well as pitch. Not heard by me.

v10 98.16 (seeds 0/11 98.16/98.12 vs v9 98.10/98.07): THE TIMING ANNEALS TOO. Everything in Annealing is bound to the temperature - the notes, their tuning, their slides, which drums play - except where the drums land: they were always dead on the sixteenth grid, even while the search was at its wildest. Now the time anneals as well: while hot, every drum hit lands off its step by a random amount scaled by the temperature (up to about a 32nd either way, the downbeat only ever late), so the hot machine stumbles and rushes; as it cools its time tightens; converged it is metronomic, machine time arrived at rather than assumed. The same hits, on their own dice; only where they land moves. Not heard by me.

v11 98.10 (seeds 0/11 98.10/98.06, level with v10 98.16/98.12), kept on judgment: THE BASS ANNEALS TOO. The last part of Annealing that ignored the temperature was the bass: an octave pulse in eighths, the machine's oldest bass line, from the first bar to the last. Now it searches with everything else: hot, its notes are chosen step by step at random - sixteenths appear, eighths drop out, the octave flips - and as the search cools it settles into the pulse; converged, it is the plain octave eighths again, arrived at. On its own dice, so nothing else moves. Not heard by me.

v12 98.33 (seeds 0/11 98.33/98.28 vs v11 98.10/98.06): A FULLER POWER-ON. t6 ends warm and low, home on C, and Annealing opened thin and distant - the radio hum alone, quiet, the room's low A arriving a bar and a half in; against t6's tail the opening was 6-12 dB short below 140 Hz. Now the radio comes in nearer full strength (+3 dB) and the room's low A hum enters three beats sooner and a little stronger, so the record steps from t6's last chord into the machine's hum without falling into a hole. The seam's spectral distance 5.2 -> 3.6 dB, flow 72 -> 78. Not heard by me.

v13 98.34 (seeds 0/11 98.34/98.23, level with v12 98.33/98.28), kept on Harry's ear (his note on t1: oblique words, not cliche). Annealing's one sung phrase, at convergence, was 'there you are, you were always here' - a plain, familiar line. Now the voice sings the found riff to 'the glass remembers how it cooled': annealing's own image (glass is annealed: cooled slowly so it keeps no strain), sideways and specific, on the same slowed riff in 5-limit just intonation over the electric piano. Not heard by me.

v14 98.33 (seeds 0/11 98.33/98.23, level with v13 98.34/98.23), kept on Harry's ear (his note on t1: it repeats a lot). Annealing's voice read the search's error aloud eight times - every epoch, convergence, the reheat and the coda. Now it reads it five: the first, third and fifth epochs (hot over the radio, nearer, nearly clear), 'zero' at convergence with the glass phrase, and the reheat's jump; the coda's last 'zero' is left to the instruments. Fewer numbers, each one news. A removal round. Not heard by me.

v15 98.32 (seeds 0/11 98.32/98.22, level with v14 98.33/98.23), kept on judgment. ROUND TYPE: section - window 3 (1:06-1:39, the second epoch), flagged static and little new against the window before (since v14 the voice no longer reads the error there). THE MACHINE LISTENS TO ITSELF: halfway through the epoch the band - pad, bass and drums - drops away for two bars and the sequencer plays its current candidate alone over the hum, still sliding and crushed, the search auditioning what it has so far; then everything comes back in on the downbeat. The parts are written as before and lifted out afterwards, so no other bar changes: against the old render window 3 moves 0.23 and every other window 0.013 or less. Not heard by me.

v16 98.32 (seeds 0/11 98.32/98.22, level with v15 98.32/98.22), kept on judgment. ROUND TYPE: section - window 7 (3:18-3:51, the middle of the last and longest epoch), flagged static and little new against the window before. GLIMPSES: there, before the search has found anything, the electric piano that will play the answer lets slip a few of its notes - the target's first two, exact and quiet, in their places in the bar; four bars later the first three; then four; then the first phrase - the answer showing through the search before the search reaches it, so convergence arrives as a recognition. Local by the note-aware map: window 7 residual -16.6 dB, every other window -59.5 or quieter. (Lesson for all: appending notes to an existing track moved every later note's per-note randomness - my first try changed windows 8-10 by -6 dB residual; giving the new notes their own track, listed last, kept everything else bit-near-identical.) Not heard by me.

v17 98.40 (seeds 0/11 98.40/98.28 vs v16 98.32/98.22). ROUND TYPE: palette - two instruments changed. THE BED ON TAPE: the pad was the album's additive 'partial' (four songs share it); now it is tape-replay strings (mellotron-strings, which no other track uses) - band-limited saws on a wobbling tape, a warm, slightly unstable bed for a song about heat. THE ANSWER SPEAKS: the electric piano that lets slip the glimpses and then plays the found riff under the sung words runs through an envelope wah, the engine's wah and the album's first - each struck note opens the band-pass and lets it fall, so the riff the voice sings has a mouth of its own. First try (strings -14 dB, wah mix 0.85) put 7 dB too much at 1.2-1.6 kHz and seed 11 lost variety (93.23); tamed, spectrum rose 97.6 -> 98.6. Not heard by me.

v18 98.30 (seeds 0/11 98.30/98.19, level with v17 98.40/98.28), kept on judgment - chirp-eco's album overview: Annealing spanned only 2.7 dB window to window, the flattest on the album, and wanted a breath. ROUND TYPE: section - window 6 (2:45-3:18, the turn from the fourth epoch to the fifth), flagged little new. THE QUENCH AND THE LAST FIRING: the furnace door opens - for four bars the band falls away to almost nothing, the search's blips alone and half as loud over the hum, where the fifth reading ('nearly clear') now lands in near-silence - and then the last, longest epoch builds back from that nothing a layer a bar: the hats, then the bass, then the strings and the backbeat, then the kick, and on the fifth bar everything. Window 6 residual -4.5 dB, motion 0.074 -> 0.119, level -1.2 dB over the window; the rest moved only by the master's gain (-43 dB). Not heard by me.

v19 98.25 (seeds 0/11 98.25/98.13, level with v18 98.30/98.19), kept on judgment. ROUND TYPE: whole song. THE HARMONY ANNEALS TOO - against Harry's 'it repeats a lot': Annealing's four chords (A minor, F, C, G in just intonation) turned in the same order for five and a half minutes while everything above them searched. Now the progression is searched as well: while the machine is hot each chord change jumps to any of the others at random, with the temperature as the chance (the opening runs C, G, C, F, C, F, G), and the loop's order emerges only as it cools; converged, the harmony settles into a cadence - F, G, then A minor - and stays home on A minor through the reheat, thirteen bars. Not heard by me.

v20 97.86 (seeds 0/11 97.86/97.75 vs v19 98.25/98.13), kept on judgment - a palette round that actually changes the sound. ROUND TYPE: palette. THE BASS CHURNS: the bass was the moog-seq, the same patch as the search's blips - one instrument doing two jobs. Now it is a Reese: two detuned saw pairs drifting against each other over a sine sub, so the low end beats and churns like something heated, and even the octave pulse it settles into when cold keeps drifting a little - the one part of the machine that never quite stops moving. The -0.4 is spectrum: the Reese is lighter than the moog in 80-160 Hz (it sits at -5 dB, lp 1.2 kHz, +3 dB at 110 Hz; louder, its churn split seed 0 into 22 sections). Also tried and dropped: the search on a plucked synth (arp-pluck) - its ping-pong scattered the song into 23 sections (87.1), and even dry it thinned the body (variety 84, cohesion 92); the search stays on the moog. Not heard by me.

v21 97.81 (seeds 0/11 97.81/97.67, level with v20 97.86/97.75), kept on judgment. ROUND TYPE: whole song (taken over the drawn type on chirp-eco's flashlight: after the intro the song sat within 1.2 dB for five minutes, the album's flattest). THE HEAT IS LOUD: the song's energy now follows the physics - hot is loud, and as the search cools the whole machine really cools. A master gain lane after the compressor, one point a bar: +0.5 dB through the hot first epochs, falling through the cooling ones to -2.5, a clear -2 for the convergence (the voice and the found riff on top), a +1.5 dB flare for the reheat - heat, briefly, again - and then the cold crystal of the coda sinking to -7. compscore's level range 7.2 -> 10.3 dB. A deeper arc (to -4.5 and -9) cost the joins (flow 74 -> 68-72) and was left. Not heard by me.

v22 97.80 (seeds 0/11 97.80/97.92, level with v21 97.81/97.67), kept on judgment. ROUND TYPE: whole song. THE LAST EPOCH TIGHTENED - against Harry's 'it repeats a lot': the fifth epoch was the longest, 28 bars, and near the target the search played its almost-answer for nearly a minute before it converged. Now it is 20 bars: the quench and the layer-by-layer build at its start are kept, the glimpses of the answer come every four bars from its sixth bar (two notes, three, four, the phrase), the cooling schedule compresses to match, and convergence arrives sixteen seconds sooner - 5:06 now, still inside the brief. The readings written against the old form move up with it. Not heard by me.

v23 97.86 (seeds 0/11 97.86/97.91 vs v22 97.80/97.92). ROUND TYPE: whole song. THE LAST FIRING, A FOURTH HIGHER - the song's ending: after the reheat the machine used to cool back into the same answer in the same key and fade, a second ending that told us nothing new. Now when it cools for the last time it settles a just fourth (4/3) above where it found its answer the first time: in the coda the strings, the Reese, the search and the electric piano all move up into D minor (the cadence now B-flat, C, D minor), and the voice sings 'the glass remembers how it cooled' once more, up there, over the cooling band - not the same answer found twice, but the same shape found somewhere new, the lift a last chorus gets. Not heard by me.

v24 97.84 (seeds 0/11 97.84/97.87, level with v23 97.86/97.91), kept on judgment. ROUND TYPE: whole song. THE READINGS SAY WHAT THE NUMBER MEANS - the voice that runs through the whole song (Harry: oblique words, not cliche; and his t1 note on the tune, which taught that half-sung takes sit between notes). The voice used to read bare numbers, half-melodized as it cooled. Now each reading is the number and then a few words on what that temperature is like: 'zero point eight six, and it takes the worse road gladly' (hot, the search accepts worse answers on purpose), 'zero point six six, it has started to keep things', then 'zero point two eight, nearly' - sung exactly, in A minor, rising and falling to end on the B a step above the A it has not reached yet - then 'zero' at convergence, and the reheat's 'zero point eight eight, shaken loose again'. The hot readings are plainly spoken over the off-station radio; nothing sits between speech and song any more. Not heard by me.

v25 97.83 (seeds 0/11 97.83/97.90, level with v24 97.84/97.87), kept on judgment. ROUND TYPE: section - window 2 (0:33-1:06, the hottest epoch's middle), flagged static and most like the power-up before it (0.15). THE ANSWER WAS ALWAYS IN THE ROOM: while the search flails at its hottest - random blips sliding into random pitches over random chords - a cello plays the very thing it is looking for: the target riff, an octave down and slowed sixteen times, one sixteenth to a bar, so it is a long, patient chorale line (A, C, E, D, C, A, G, E, G, A, held one to three bars each, in the song's just intonation) that nobody could hear as the riff yet. When the search finds the riff three minutes later, the ear has heard its shape once already, as a slow song - and the hot epoch has something to follow. Window 2 residual -12.5 dB (clearly changed), window 3 -42 (the last note's hall), every other -57 dB. Not heard by me.

v26 97.90 (seeds 0/11 97.90/97.96 vs v25 97.83/97.90; spectrum 94.1 -> 94.8). ROUND TYPE: whole song. THE TEMPERATURE, AUDIBLE: the song is a simulated-annealing search, a random walk whose step size is a temperature - and Xenakis's dynamic stochastic synthesis (GENDY, 1991; wM's new gendyn layer) is the same idea as sound: each wave cycle a polygon whose corners random-walk by a step size. So under everything now runs an open fifth (A and E) on gendyn whose step sizes ARE the song's temperature, read bar by bar from the schedule: while the machine is hot the corners and segment lengths wander far and the drone slides and frays into glissando clouds; as it cools the steps shrink and the tone settles; converged, the walk all but stops and the waveform freezes into one steady, grainy tone; the reheat shakes it loose again, and in the coda it moves up the fourth with the band. The search's state is now something you hear in the timbre of the floor, not only in the notes above it. Every window moved by about -9 dB residual (a new layer through the whole song). Not heard by me.

v27 97.92 (seeds 0/11 97.92/97.97 vs v26 97.90/97.96). ROUND TYPE: section - window 3 (1:06-1:39, the second epoch), flagged little new against the window before. THE DRUMS FIND A RULE FIRST: while hot, the drums were noise - every step of every piece sampled at random, the same in the second epoch as in the first. Now through the second epoch (around the two bars where the machine listens to itself) the kick keeps its place and everything else is played by a Game of Life (wM's life system): a glider crossing a sixteen-by-four torus, one generation a bar, whose live cells pick snare, clave, cowbell and hat, bottom row low - a small shape that keeps moving, so the pattern slides and turns over bar by bar instead of scattering. The kit finds a rule before the notes do, and the second epoch sounds unlike the first (sparser: density -1.5). After the listening bars the glider runs on HighLife's rule (B36/S23). Window 3 residual -11.9 dB, change against window 2 0.54 -> 0.64 (no longer 'little new'); window 4 -53 (tails), every other -75 dB. Not heard by me.

v28 98.17 (seeds 0/11 98.17/98.23 vs v27 97.92/97.97; the song's best; spectrum 95.0 -> 97.7). ROUND TYPE: palette. THE SEARCH ON A HOME COMPUTER: the search itself - the blips that wander, glide and finally lock onto the riff - was a Berlin-school Moog sequencer voice, a saw through a resonant filter. Now it is Casio CZ phase distortion (1984, the home computer's synth; wM's pd layer, pinned this morning): a sine whose phase is bent into a resonant saw with no filter at all. Each blip starts with its resonance up (an envelope on the bend) and the temperature adds more, so hot the search chirps and glitters and cold it rounds off toward a plain tone - the CZ's own sweep doing what the filter did, with a square an octave below for body. And a sub: compscore's new signed spectrum detail (chirp-eco, from chirper-three) showed the worst band was a DEFICIT, 38 Hz 9 dB short of the album - so a sine an octave under the bass's root now holds one long note a bar wherever the bass is heard (out of the quench, the listening bars and the power-up; up the fourth in the coda). Not heard by me.

v29 98.17 (seeds 0/11 98.17/98.23, level with v28 98.17/98.23). ROUND TYPE: section - window 8 (3:51-4:24, the converged section's second half into the reheat), flagged little new against the window before. THE SLOW SONG CATCHES UP: in the hottest epoch a cello played the target riff sixteen times slower - a chorale nobody could hear as the riff. Now, once the search has found it, under the second sung phrase of the converged section the cello comes back with the same line only eight times slower: two steps a bar over the cadence (F, G, A minor, A minor, twice - chord tones, a ninth, a suspended fourth), eight bars, ending on the A as the reheat breaks in. The slow song and the fast riff together - the answer heard at two speeds at once, and the first minute of the song recalled at its resolution. Window 8 residual -15.7 dB (clearly changed), every other window -64 dB or below. Not heard by me.

v30 98.20 (seeds 0/11 98.20/98.25 vs v29 98.17/98.23; the song's best). ROUND TYPE: whole song. THE CLOCK ANNEALS: everything in this song anneals - the notes, the chords, the bass, the drums' timing, the drone's timbre - except the clock. Now the tempo is a random walk scaled by the temperature too: hot, the whole band's time drifts and lurches together, gliding bar to bar up to about seven beats a minute either side of 116 (roughly 110 to 123 in the first epoch), leaning ahead and dragging behind; as the machine cools the drift shrinks, and from convergence it holds 116 exactly - the steadiness itself is the arrival. The reheat shakes it loose again and the coda settles. The power-up keeps strict time so the hand-over from t6 is unchanged (letting it drift there cost the joins 4 points). Folded in: compscore's bands found the bass 9 dB short at 83 Hz, so the Reese has a little more E2 weight (spectrum 97.7 -> 98.7). Length 5:06. Not heard by me.

v31 98.44 (seeds 0/11 98.44/98.40 vs v30 re-scored now 98.39 on seed 0 - v30 measured 98.20 an hour ago; the album's neighbours moved its flow term 72.6 -> 78.0 since). ROUND TYPE: palette. THE POWER SUPPLY SETTLES: the song opens with the machine powering up over a hum - the library's evolving drone. Now over it, on the same A, comes the machine's power supply: an audio-rate Rossler attractor (wM's chaos layer, its buzzy z axis: a spike train like mains through a transformer) whose control starts high and decays over eighteen seconds, so the supply comes in unstable and frayed - chaotic, then period-doubled, a shadow an octave down - and settles into one steady electrical tone before the search begins. A song about a system settling now begins with a smaller one. Tried first as the whole hum: the drone's low-mid body carries the joins with t6 and t8 (flow 72 -> 44 without it), so it stays underneath. Window 1 residual -20 dB, the rest -93 dB. Not heard by me.

v32 98.44 (seeds 0/11 98.44/98.40, level with v31 98.44/98.40). ROUND TYPE: section - window 9 (4:24-5:07, the reheat's end and the coda), flagged static. THE CRYSTAL: annealing is how metal grows its crystals - one cell repeated at every scale. The coda had the cooled band simply restating the found riff a fourth higher. Now, in its last eight bars, once the search has found its answer again, the answer is heard at three scales at once: the keys at its own speed, a VOSIM bell (wM's vosim-bell) an octave up at half speed, and the cello - which played the riff sixteen times slower through the hottest epoch, eight times slower at convergence - now only four times slower. A mensuration canon of the found riff: the slow song has nearly caught up, and the lattice rings to the end. Window 9 residual -21.5 dB; every other window -77 dB. Not heard by me.

v33 98.44 (seeds 0/11 98.44/98.41, level with v32 98.44/98.40). ROUND TYPE: section - window 2 (0:33-1:06, the hottest epoch's middle), flagged static. THE WORSE ROAD, GLADLY: the first reading says the hot machine 'takes the worse road gladly' - that is the Metropolis rule, the heart of annealing: hot, it accepts moves that make its answer worse. Through the hottest epoch's middle every such move it takes is now heard as itself, on the very step where it happens: a small CZ phase-distortion voice slides from the step's old note down or up to the worse one it has just chosen - a slip, a shrug, louder the worse the move - thirteen of them over sixteen bars, an octave under the search, with a short echo. The better moves stay silent. The search itself is untouched (the moves are only noted as they happen; nothing new is drawn). Window 2 residual -21 dB, every other window -63 dB or lower. Not heard by me.

v34 98.45 (seeds 0/11 98.45/98.42 vs v33 98.44/98.41; the song's best). ROUND TYPE: whole song. THE SONG FINDS ITS WORDS - after Harry's ring note on t1 ('the singing came a long way ... keep hillclimbing it'), the same lesson here: when the search converges, the voice that read the error aloud sings - but it sang one line three times. Now each time is a new line on the same tune: 'the glass remembers how it cooled'; then 'the wrong roads are kept in its shape' (every worse move it took is in the answer it found); and in the coda, a just fourth higher, 'and holds the heat it gave away' - that last one in two parts, a second voice a diatonic third above in the same just intonation, a hair behind, on the other side: the crystal sung as a chord. New takes: chirp tts --sing on the same melody, humanize 0.35. Not heard by me.

v35 98.44 (seeds 0/11 98.44/98.40, level with v34 98.45/98.42), kept on judgment. ROUND TYPE: section - window 3 (1:06-1:39, the second epoch), flagged little new against the window before. PARALLEL TEMPERING: annealing has a sibling trick - run a second copy of the search hotter than the first, and now and then let it take the colder one's answer (replica exchange). Through the second epoch's first sixteen bars a replica does exactly that, out loud: it starts from where the search is, runs hotter on its own dice (the main search untouched), and every four bars, if its answer is worse, it takes the main one's - so a second line, plucked on a Karplus-Strong string (1983, the first plucked string a computer made: noise in a one-period loop, wM's ks, pinned today), wanders off from the sequencer in eighths, snaps into unison with it, and drifts away again. It took the main answer twice: once in the two bars where the machine listens to itself - so there the two searches are heard alone together, agreeing - and again four bars later.
